queries: SELECT tick, income_tax_revenue, property_tax_revenue, utility_revenue, transit_revenue, road_spend, water_sewer_spend, balance, debt, treasury FROM budget_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 12
SELECT tick, demand_kw, supply_kw, outage_fraction, contract_mode, tariff FROM power_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 12
SELECT tick, capacity, demand, load_ratio, failure_rate FROM water_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 12
SELECT tick, AVG(condition_score) AS avg_condition, AVG(occupancy) AS avg_occupancy, AVG((power_served::int)) AS power_rate FROM building_monthly GROUP BY tick ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 6
SELECT tick, AVG(congestion) AS congestion, AVG(wear) AS wear, AVG(travel_time) AS travel_time FROM road_monthly r JOIN commute_monthly c USING (run_id,tick) GROUP BY tick ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 6

SELECT tick, AVG(satisfaction) AS satisfaction, AVG(disposable_income) AS disposable_income, AVG((employed::int)) AS employment, COUNT(*) AS population FROM citizen_monthly GROUP BY tick ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 6
turns.rationale: The main failures are severe road deterioration (wear 0.97, congestion 0.78), highly volatile power outages (19–40%), and an elevated but not yet failing water load (0.85). The city has a strong treasury and surplus, so I will fund repairs and capacity rather than raise taxes. I’m also reducing transit and electricity costs to support satisfaction while switching power procurement away from spot exposure.
